paperInfo.subject: Social Science
paperInfo.paperName: Grade 7 Social Science Paper 1 (Practice - Multiple Choice)

questions.questionText: Which relative belongs to a person's extended family?
questions.explanation: An uncle is part of the extended family, while mother, father and sister belong to the nuclear family.

questions.questionText: A family in which a child takes care of younger siblings after the death of both parents is called a
questions.explanation: A child-headed family is one where a child, usually the eldest sibling, takes on responsibility for the household.

questions.questionText: Which action shows respect for an elder in Zimbabwean culture?

options.text: greeting them politely and kneeling where customary

questions.explanation: Greeting elders politely, and kneeling in cultures where this is customary, shows respect.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps build cooperation between families in a rural community?
questions.explanation: Nhimbe/ilima brings community members together to help each other with farm or household tasks.

questions.questionText: A family with one husband and more than one wife is called a
questions.explanation: A polygamous family has one spouse married to more than one partner, typically one husband with multiple wives.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a responsibility a Grade 7 learner has at home?
questions.explanation: Learners are expected to help with age-appropriate chores as part of their family responsibilities.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps prevent tooth decay?

options.text: eating a lot of sugary sweets

questions.explanation: Regular brushing removes plaque and food particles that cause tooth decay.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a communicable disease?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by bacteria and can spread from person to person, making it communicable.

questions.questionText: Failing to provide a child with food and shelter violates the child's right to
questions.explanation: Food and shelter fall under a child's right to an adequate standard of living.

questions.questionText: Hitting or beating a child is a form of
questions.explanation: Physical abuse involves causing bodily harm, such as hitting or beating.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a healthy lifestyle practice?
questions.explanation: Regular physical exercise supports overall physical and mental health.

questions.questionText: Immunising babies mainly helps to
questions.explanation: Immunisation protects infants by building resistance against specific infectious diseases.

questions.questionText: One effect of HIV and AIDS on communities is an increase in
questions.explanation: HIV and AIDS can leave children without parents, increasing the number of child-headed households.

questions.questionText: Jesus Christ's followers who travelled with him and learned from him were called
questions.explanation: The twelve close followers of Jesus Christ are referred to as his disciples.

questions.questionText: In Christianity, baptism mainly symbolises

options.text: cleansing from sin and entry into the faith

questions.explanation: Baptism symbolises spiritual cleansing and initiation into the Christian faith.

questions.questionText: The holy book of Judaism, containing its foundational laws and teachings, is called the
questions.explanation: The Torah is the central sacred text of Judaism.

questions.questionText: Jews traditionally gather to worship in a building called a
questions.explanation: Jewish communal worship traditionally takes place in a synagogue.

questions.questionText: Which of the Five Pillars of Islam involves travelling to Mecca?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims are expected to undertake at least once if able.

questions.questionText: In Indigenous Religion, a person who communicates with ancestral spirits on behalf of the family or community is called a
questions.explanation: A spirit medium or n'anga is believed to communicate with ancestral spirits.

questions.questionText: A ceremony held about a year after a death, believed to welcome the deceased's spirit back as an ancestor, is called
questions.explanation: Kurova guva is the ceremony performed to formally welcome a deceased person's spirit back as a family ancestor.

questions.questionText: Which symbol is closely associated with Christianity?
questions.explanation: The Cross represents Jesus Christ's crucifixion and is a central Christian symbol.

questions.questionText: Which pre-colonial state is associated with the building of Great Zimbabwe?
questions.explanation: The Torwa State is associated with building and later occupying the Great Zimbabwe monument complex in its later period, alongside earlier Shona builders.

questions.questionText: Zimbabwe's national coat of arms includes an animal known for representing keen eyesight and vigilance. Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: Kudus appear on Zimbabwe's coat of arms as supporters, often associated with alertness and grace.

questions.questionText: The first Chimurenga/Umvukela was mainly a reaction against
questions.explanation: The first Chimurenga/Umvukela arose largely in resistance to colonial occupation and the loss of land.

questions.questionText: Which national holiday specifically honours the contribution of soldiers?
questions.explanation: Defence Forces Day is set aside to recognise the role and sacrifice of the armed forces.

questions.questionText: A traditional court where community disputes are resolved by elders or a chief is called a
questions.explanation: The dare/inkundla is a traditional/customary community gathering used to resolve disputes.

questions.questionText: Great Zimbabwe and Khami are both examples of
questions.explanation: Both Great Zimbabwe and Khami are stone-walled monuments built by pre-colonial Zimbabwean states.

questions.questionText: A child adopted by Zimbabwean parents and formally registered as Zimbabwean gains citizenship by
questions.explanation: Citizenship gained through a formal legal registration process (such as after adoption) is citizenship by registration.

questions.questionText: A leader who allows workers to make most decisions with little supervision is practising
questions.explanation: Allowing followers to participate freely in decisions reflects democratic or participatory leadership.

questions.questionText: A legal document used to state how a deceased person's property should be shared is called a
questions.explanation: A will is the legal document specifying how a person's estate should be distributed after death.

questions.questionText: Writing or drawing on public walls without permission is called
questions.explanation: Unauthorised writing/drawing on walls or public property is known as graffiti.

questions.questionText: In the traditional leadership hierarchy in Zimbabwe, who holds the highest authority?
questions.explanation: In the traditional hierarchy, the chief holds authority over headmen, village heads and family heads.

questions.questionText: Neighbours forming a group to watch over each other's homes and property is an example of
questions.explanation: A neighbourhood watch committee is a community-based group formed to improve security.

questions.questionText: Burning coal for energy mainly contributes to
questions.explanation: Burning coal releases smoke and gases into the atmosphere, causing air pollution.

questions.questionText: The replanting of trees in an area that had trees before is called
questions.explanation: Reforestation specifically refers to replanting trees where forest previously existed.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a way of overcoming desertification?

options.text: planting trees and grass to cover bare soil

questions.explanation: Planting vegetation helps stabilise soil and reverse the spread of desert-like conditions.

questions.questionText: A build-up of litter such as plastic bottles and papers in an open area is an example of
questions.explanation: Solid waste scattered on land is a form of land pollution.

questions.questionText: Which method is traditionally used to make a woven basket?
questions.explanation: Baskets are traditionally made by weaving materials such as reeds or grass together.

questions.questionText: Which organisation is mainly responsible for administering football in Zimbabwe?
questions.explanation: ZIFA (Zimbabwe Football Association) is the governing body for football/soccer in Zimbabwe.

questions.questionText: A road sign showing people walking is meant to warn drivers of
questions.explanation: A pedestrian symbol on a road sign warns drivers to watch for people, often children, crossing the road.
